members.authored_reason: Twelve bytes of an asar prefix. The reader needs sixteen before any field is meaningful, so the correct outcome is a refusal that names the truncation rather than a parse of whatever follows.

A sixteen-byte asar prefix whose three pickle fields agree with each other but declare a 1024-byte header inside a 64-byte file. Every internal consistency check passes, so only a check against the real file length can reject it.

A PE32+ image whose .text section spans RVA 0x1000..0x2000 and whose .data section starts at RVA 0x1800. One address maps to two sections, so any address-to-bytes answer would be arbitrary and the reader must refuse instead of picking one.

A romfs file node whose next-header offset is its own offset. The linked list closes on itself. The one real node is recoverable, so the correct outcome is exactly one file rather than a refusal or an unbounded walk.

A romfs directory whose first-child offset is the directory itself. Descending it re-enters the same node forever unless a depth bound stops the walk. The image holds no file node, so the correct outcome is zero files and a terminating walk.
An empty file handed to the zip extractor. The refusal must identify the empty input instead of collapsing it into a missing-directory error.

reason.equals: DR-BINFMT-0003: zip parse failed: the input is empty, so it holds no archive

members.authored_reason: A stored zip entry whose directory declares 1 MiB of output from 64 compressed bytes, an expansion ratio of 16384 against a cap of 100. The lie is in the declared sizes, so the quota drops the member before any byte is decompressed, records the refusal, and publishes no expanding payload.

violations: zip-quota `bomb.bin`: DR-BINFMT-0009: extraction quota exceeded on entry `bomb.bin`: per-entry expansion ratio 16384 exceeds cap 100

members.authored_reason: A uzip header declaring 4294967294 blocks in a 168-byte file. The table of contents that count implies is 32 GiB, so the reader must reject the count against the real file length before it reserves anything.

reason.contains: TOC of 4294967295 offsets runs past end of image

members.authored_reason: A zip end-of-central-directory record declaring 65534 entries with an empty central directory. The refusal must name the unsatisfied count and must not mistake 65534 for the reserved ZIP64 sentinel 65535.

reason.equals: DR-BINFMT-0003: zip parse failed: the end-of-central-directory record declares 65534 entries, but the central directory contains 0

members.authored_reason: Four bytes of zip magic in front of an ELF header. Classification by magic alone names it a zip, so recovery must refuse with the exact missing-directory reason while preserving the detected kind.

reason.equals: DR-BINFMT-0003: zip parse failed: no end-of-central-directory record in the last 256 byte(s), so this is not a zip archive whatever its leading bytes say

members.authored_reason: A structurally valid zip that holds nothing: a 22-byte end-of-central-directory record and no entries. Refusing it would be wrong, so the correct outcome is a recovery of exactly zero entries with no integrity violation.

A zip whose only entry is named ../escape.txt. The archive is otherwise well formed, so the extractor must keep going, drop the entry, and record why. The correct outcome is zero entries written and one named zip-slip violation, and the harness separately proves nothing landed outside the extraction root.

violations: zip-slip `../escape.txt`: DR-BINFMT-0008: archive entry path escapes container root: ../escape.txt

members.authored_reason: A squashfs superblock with valid magic and a major version of 7. The reader implements majors 1 through 4. Guessing a layout for an unknown version would produce plausible wrong output, so the correct outcome is a refusal that names the version.
